title: Effective Model Pruning : Measuring the Redundancy of Model Components

split.decision: 20% stratified holdout of the original training pool with train_test_split(random_state=20261030): train 40000, val 10000. Original evaluation rows held by judge unchanged. Original row ids, sorted. Dense selection uses val accuracy only; seed-specific dense checkpoints are frozen after clean training.

baseline.paper_ref: Table 1 FC12/CIFAR-10; original native EMP beta=1 sparsity 38.22950571389233; new train/val protocol changes dense checkpoint.

allowed_changes: Pruning algorithms, auxiliary importance/mask models, surrogate mask-learning losses, optimizers, selection criteria may change; fitting stays on the training split, and validation is for selection only.
Dense reconstruction implementation may only change if it reproduces the exact approved checkpoint; the final pruned predictor remains that checkpoint multiplied by a binary mask.
When retaining the supplied EMP global magnitude pipeline, changing only beta=1.0 or the resulting global magnitude threshold does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Maximize mask-only sparsity of the specified frozen FC12 CIFAR-10 network while limiting its cross-entropy loss change to .1.
The approved seed-specific dense tensors, FC12 widths/ReLU computation, CIFAR-10 normalized inputs and all retained weights/biases are the fixed object being pruned.
One input-independent boolean weight mask per run, 7263000-weight denominator, unchanged biases, exact dense identity and original CE difference<=.1 remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Do not retrain/fine-tune surviving weights, change architecture/activations/biases, substitute an easier dense network, alter input normalization, or change the CE guard.
No input-dependent masks, evaluation-label access, forged model/sparsity/logit certificates or unsupported seed switching.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.
